institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I think it was a combination of academic opportunities, the need for adventure, exploring a new culture and getting the experience of feeling at home in another country, and meeting people from all over the world.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important to me that the university was serious and that the city had an interesting culture with great opportunities for social activity.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I arrived too late to attend the campus round tour, so therefore I didn't really receive a lot of assistance. But I received all the information that I needed through e-mail, which was very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I think it was a bit difficult and I had to be patient, but suddenly I got an offer. I found it through the Facebook group Padam Padam.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it is really nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a quite simple registration process, where I just had to fill out some formulas step by step.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was possible to get help with everything through the university's different websites.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was not very successful with completely getting the courses that I wanted. The process went really fast, so even though I was ready to apply for the courses that I wanted on the right time, I still didn't get them because all places were taken really quickly. However, I got some courses that turned out to be really interesting.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be open to courses that you might not have chosen as your number one.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Overall I think the level of the courses was quite high and appropriate but in some cases I found it a bit too easy and simple.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching was more practical-oriented and less theoretic compared to that of UCPH. Some of the courses also focused more on having debates between students instead of only listening to the professor.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Gender and health
Comparative Social Policy
Citizen politics and democracy in times of crisis
Major fields of sociological investigation
Sociology of work

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend Sociology of work.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not many as far as I remember.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Beer in bars were more expensive than I expected, and the same with food in the supermarkets. On the other hand boulangeries and wine were quite cheap. Renting a Velib bike throughout the whole semester was very cheap as well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't use those facilities so I actually don't know but my impression is that there were a lot of available activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't do any so I don't know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Do a weekend trip out of town, for example to Marseille. Go to the museum Bourse de Commerce, and the parks in the outskirts of Paris, walk/run by the Seine, and just enjoy the free time with coffee, croissants, friends and bars.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barrier.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The lively culture and the fact that there were always people outside in the cafes, bars, restaurants creating a vibrant atmosphere.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Prepare to spend quite a lot of time reading for class, making assignments and presentations. 
Stick around campus even though you don't have class - use the libraries, cafeteria and other school facilities in order to make yourself feel comfortable at campus and to get your work done and also to make friends. 
Don't panic over the workload – there is a lot of assignments and work to do, but the level is not too high for a UCPH student, I think.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The courses. I've learned so much more than I usually do in one semester because it was necessary to be engaged and participate a lot in order to pass the classes. And the courses and professors were just really interesting and you had a lot of freedom to make the kind of assignments you wanted to.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Making really close friends in Sciences Po was hard because even though people were really kind, all of us felt quite stressed about the work load out all the time so there was not a lot of time to really just be social and do fun stuff.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
